To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the health dimension is not sufficiently addressed in existing global scenario analyses and that it is possible to link global developments to future health.

health is an outcome of the interaction between the sociocultural (e.g. lifestyle, education), economic (e.g. income, employment, poverty), and ecological (e.g. environmental pollution, climate change) determinants of health and that these determinants of health are not consistently addressed in the global scenario studies.

future health is determined by multiple driving forces, that these driving forces can be identified and described in existing scenarios, and that the resulting health outcomes can be described in a comprehensive way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the health of the world population might be affected by global changes.
the question of how to deal with health in global scenario studies and how to link the different driving forces of health.
a better understanding of the future of health in the context of global changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the health dimension has not been given the attention it deserves in global scenario studies, but that it could be included in a consistent and useful way.
health in the future depends on the future developments of sociocultural, ecological, and economic factors.
the future is not only about health, it is about health in a world with multiple driving forces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the future of health is closely linked to the future of the planet, and that the future of both is in the hands of humans.
the global scenario studies reviewed in this paper do provide a good description of the future health developments, but only when the different scenario studies are combined.
the future of health is a complex and multidimensional issue that needs to be addressed in a comprehensive way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

future health is not an independent scenario variable, but rather an outcome of multiple driving forces, and that it can be incorporated into existing global scenario studies by linking the different scenarios of the driving forces to potential future health developments.
health is not a single dimension, but a complex, multidimensional phenomenon.
health should be incorporated in global scenario studies as an important outcome of multiple driving forces, and not just as a separate scenario.
